newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB ends Tokyo near day's high, supported at 122.40.
newsitem.headline: JGB ends Tokyo near day's high, supported at 122.40.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended near the day's high in Tokyo on Friday, as day traders quickly moved to cover short positions after it failed to crack support at 122.40.
The December rebounded strongly after briefly falling to 122.40 where its strong chart support lies. It ended at 122.84 after moving between 122.40 to 122.85.
"Day traders, being reluctant to pile up positions ahead of general elections (on Sunday), rushed to cover positions as soon as the December hit 122.40," said a European bank trader.
Recent voter surveys have showed that Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's LDP party is likely to win a simple majority in the 500-seat Lower House of parliament.

"The results of the elections are unlikely to influence bond prices immediately. But, what we would like to see is if the new government can put in place a large supplementary budget which would only further aggravate the budget balance," said a city bank trader. Balancing the budget has been one of Hashimoto's policy priorities.
U.S. hedge funds appear to have sold the December, while buying up Japanese stock futures on SIMEX, traders said.
In the cash market, city banks unloaded non-government yen debt, dampening JGB sentiment, traders said.
The Ministry of Finance is expected to offer 10-year JGBs on Tuesday with a prospective 2.9 percent coupon.
Brokers have lightened their inventories ahead of the auction. The market is normally depressed in the run-up to an auction as participants seek a higher coupon on a new issue, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.805 percent at 0709 GMT, down from 2.825 percent on Thursday. Gains in the other JGB sectors were limited.
The market is keen to see if the funds set up to clear up the bad loan mess of failed mortgage firms will tap the JGB auctions due next week, traders said.

The ministry is also expected to offer six-year notes on Thursday. The funds are said to be waiting for a chance to invest in bonds, while temporarily parking a large amount of money in Treasury bills and certificates of deposits (CDs).
The New Financial Stabilisation Fund, one of those funds, recently allocated 750 billion yen for CDs and 50 billion yen for Treasury bills, a city bank trader said.
